sources.entry: BulkPicTools - Free browser-based bulk image workspace. Upload once, chain 40+ tools (compress, convert, crop, background removal, face blur) without re-uploading. Files never leave your device. #free

summary.name: BulkPicTools
summary.one_liner: A browser-based bulk image editor that compresses, converts, crops, resizes and runs AI image tools on many files at once, processing everything locally on your device.
keywords: free image tools no sign up
use_cases: Compress and resize a folder of photos for websites or uploads
Convert iPhone HEIC photos to JPG in bulk
Prepare product photos with removed backgrounds for Shopify or Amazon
Batch blur faces in photo albums
Generate app icon and favicon packages
Make a printable contact sheet PDF from photos
summary.what_it_does: BulkPicTools lets you drop single images, folders or ZIP archives and run batch operations such as compress, convert, crop, resize and adjust on 200+ images in one pass. Results can be chained into the next tool without downloading and re-uploading. The page lists 95 tools in total (the FAQ says 93), covering scene workflows such as app icon packages, store screenshots, contact sheets, EPUB creation and social media sizing. AI features (background removal, face blur, super-resolution, watermark removal, auto enhancement, grouping by content) are said to run locally via WebAssembly and WebGPU, with models downloaded on first use. The page states files are never sent to a server.
notable: All processing runs locally in the browser with no uploads; works offline after first load
Tool chaining: compress, convert and crop without re-uploading between steps
Local AI models (background removal, face blur, upscaling) via WebAssembly and WebGPU
Scene pages combine multiple tools into guided workflows such as app icons and store screenshots
caveats: AI models must be downloaded on first use before working offline
Page says 'Free forever' but describes no paid tier; the comparison table marks some competitor features as partial
Tool count is inconsistent on the page (95 vs 93)
Platforms other than the web browser are not clearly stated; Windows, macOS, iOS and Android are only mentioned in context of outputs/use
